requirements.statement: For each button within a form that shows a visible label, its accessible name contains at least that visible label.

citations.quote: Chaque [bouton](#bouton-formulaire) affichant un [intitulé visible](#intitule-visible) vérifie-t-il ces conditions (hors cas particuliers) ?
Pour chaque bouton, vérifier que son nom accessible contient au moins son intitulé visible ;

routes.statement: The accessible name contains the text of the visible label, where the visible label's punctuation and capital letters may be ignored; mathematical symbols may be taken literally.

citations.quote: vérifier que son nom accessible contient au moins son intitulé visible
La ponctuation et les lettres majuscules sont présentes dans le texte de l’[intitulé visible](#intitule-visible) : elles peuvent être ignorées dans le nom accessible sans porter à conséquence ;
les symboles mathématiques peuvent être repris littéralement pour servir d’étiquette au nom accessible
un « nom accessible » sera considéré comme non-pertinent s’il ne reprend pas le texte visible du bouton.

exceptions.statement: When the visible text serves as a symbol (other than a mathematical expression), the name expresses the function the symbol conveys and need not contain it literally.

citations.quote: Le texte de l’[intitulé visible](#intitule-visible) sert de symbole : le texte ne doit pas être interprété littéralement au niveau du nom accessible.
Ce cas particulier s’applique également au test 11.9.2.
Pour le test 11.9.2, voir cas particuliers critère 11.2.

requirements.statement: For each button within a form that shows a visible label, each of these that is present contains at least the visible label: the aria-label, the passage of text linked by aria-labelledby, the value of an input of type submit, reset or button, the content of a button element, the alt of an input of type image, and the title.

citations.quote: S’il est présent, le contenu de l’attribut WAI-ARIA `aria-label `contient au moins l’[intitulé visible](#intitule-visible) ;
lié au bouton via un attribut WAI-ARIA `aria-labelledby` contient au moins l’[intitulé visible](#intitule-visible) ;
S’il est présent, le contenu de l’attribut value d’une balise `<input>` de type `submit`, `reset` ou `button` contient au moins l’[intitulé visible](#intitule-visible) ;
S’il est présent, le contenu de la balise `<button>` contient au moins l’[intitulé visible](#intitule-visible) ;
S’il est présent, le contenu de l’attribut `alt` d’une balise `<input>` de type `image` contient au moins l’[intitulé visible](#intitule-visible) ;
S’il est présent, le contenu de l’attribut `title` contient au moins l’[intitulé visible](#intitule-visible).

rationale.text: The test applies to buttons within a form that show a visible label, and the glossary says a visible label may be text or an image of text. Telling whether a button shows one, and reading it when it is an image or an icon, is judgment. Deciding that a name contains the visible label also needs judgment, because the particular cases of criterion 11.2, which apply to this test, allow punctuation and capitals to be ignored and make an exception when the visible text serves as a symbol, which only a reader can recognise. The wording asks the condition of every labelling source present, and the methodology of the accessible name; the entry keeps both as requirements. So the entry stays at none. One custom check gives a hint: for a button element or an input button in a form with an aria-label and no aria-labelledby, whose visible text is plain text in a system font, it faults when no word of that text appears in the aria-label. That covers the main route for aria-label only and leaves out every other source and every button whose visible label is not plain text, so its scope is partial. Its fault is evidence only: the visible text may be a symbol, or may not be the button's whole visible label. Raising it would need a definition of the visible label that code can read for every button, and a rule for the symbol case. No axe-core rule is tagged for this test. axe-core's label-content-name-mismatch, tagged for test 6.1.5, checks that elements named from their content and given an aria-label or aria-labelledby keep their visible text in the accessible name. It is linked as evidence only, with partial scope and the main route only: it also looks at links and at buttons outside forms, which this test does not cover, it cannot apply the symbol exception, and how it extracts and compares visible text is not established here, so it gets the weakest reading. Applicability is judgment, since whether a button shows a visible label may need judgment. Needs is empty.
